full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why a direction should not be given to issue sell permission to transfer certain flats of a building at Plot No. 48 and 50, Road no. 9, DIT Rehabilitation Project (REH Zone) Badda, Dhaka to the purchasers petitioner, which was build up by a developer with permission of respondent No. 1 as permitted earlier to transfer another flat of same building to another purchaser vide Memo No. রাজউক/এ-১/বারি/বাড্ডা/০-৯-৪৮/৫১৪৮ তারিখ:২৮-১০-২০১৩ (Annexure-E series) and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the rule, in short, are that the petitioner "Transparent Homes Limited" is a company which was constituted under The Companies Act, 1994, On 10-7-2006, a deed of agreement had been concluded between the petitioner and the land owners of Plot No. 48 and 50, Merul Badda, DIT Project, South Baridhara which they got allotment from respondent No. 1, RAJUK as 99 years lessee, in respect of construction of 6-storied residential building and then the land owner executed a registered irrevocable general power of attorney being No. 15637 dated 11-7-2006 in favour of the petitioner as their legal attorney. The petitioner being empowered by the aforesaid power of attorney in pursuant of aforesaid deed of agreement obtained land use clearance certificate and approved plan from RAJUK, then, started construction work in the aforesaid land. The petitioner on the basis of power of attorney was empowered to sell flat including land in ratio to any person or any institution without having any permission of the land owners. The petitioner thereby sold out flats from his proportion to (12) Md Nazmul Islam Miah, son of late Nawab Ali Miah of 69/A, Maniknagar, Wari, Dhaka, Flat No. C-4 (4th floor), 1024.771 sft (2) Sumon Barua, son of Bramananda Barua of Unicorn Electronics, GP-27, Shahjadpur, Gulshan, Dhaka-1212, Flat No. B-02 (2nd floor), 645.964 sft (3) Md Abdul Motaleb (Dulal) son of late Md Abdul Gofur of House No. 39/A & 39/B, Flat No. B3, Road-8, Abdur Rofik Housing, Mohammadpur, Dhaka who on performing a no objection deed on 7-12-2014 sold out said flat to aforesaid Sumon Barua (4) Tahmina Ali, wife of Md Younus Ali, of 1831, East Badda, Gulshan, Dhaka-1212, Flat No. A-3(3rd Floor), 1024 sft (5) Md Zakir Hossain, son of late Ali Asraf of 57/57-A, Uday Tower, Gulshan Avenue, Gulshan-1, Dhaka-1212, Flat No. C-01 (1st floor), 1024 sft (6) Mrs. Fatema Begum, wife of Md Ibrahim Khan of Green peace, Flat No. L-14, 41, Chamelybagh, Shantinagar, Dhaka, Flat No. A-05(5th floor) 908 sft. The petitioner performed deed of agreement with the aforesaid purchasers in different dates except Tahmina Ali but provided her with money receipt of installments. The petitioner company's management being changed, Mr Mohammad Enayetullah was made managing director instead of ASM Shakhawat Ullah of Transparent Homes Ltd. The respondent No. 1 vide Memo No. রাজউক/এ-১/বারি/বাড্ডা/০-৯-৪৮/৫১৪৭ dated 28-10-2013 excepted said change in management of the company. The petitioner having received all installments from aforesaid purchasers submitted applications to the respondent No. 3 for permission to transfer those flats to the purchasers on 7-1-2015 and 19-1-2015 but till today the respondents did not permit the petitioner to transfer flats to the purchasers. It is contended that earlier respondents issued sale permission for another purchaser. Hence, they filed the instant writ petition and obtained the Rule.
